mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day S&P 500 forward return positive due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3 in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, reducing equity risk premia and pushing the S&P 500 20-day forward return negative.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in month t and t-1
failure_condition: During such triggers, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean > -0.1, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in INDPRO above 0.5% for two months indicates strengthening supply-side conditions, which tends to compress equity valuation multiples and produces a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >0.5% in month t and t-1
failure_condition: During supply expansion triggers, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (mean within ±0.05, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (household spending index) exceeding 2% above the prior month's value, in the absence of adverse macro triggers, predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate sustained demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, 20-day forward returns are not consistently positive (mean < 0.02, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates persistent policy tightness, elevating risk aversion and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean > -0.01, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 1% over two months suggests weakening hiring momentum, which tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >1% in month t and t-1
failure_condition: During such labor weakness, 20-day forward returns over the next 60 days are not consistently negative (mean > -0.02, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (goods demand) and RSAFS (retail sales) by more than 3% in a month signals resilient consumer and business demand, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >3% and RSAFS increases by >3% in the same month
failure_condition: During such interaction triggers, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (mean < 0.01, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-constrained environment when INDPRO growth lags behind CPIAUCSL inflation by >0.4 percentage points for two consecutive months tends to raise uncertainty and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth - CPIAUCSL inflation > 0.4pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such supply imbalance triggers, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (mean > -0.05, t-test p > 0.05).
